name: Acid Line
about: Squelchy resonant saw bass in the style of a TB-303: overlapping notes slide, harder notes open the filter further.

name: Sub Sine
about: Pure sine sub-bass that sits under a kick; Drive adds harmonics so it reads on small speakers.

name: Reese Bass
about: Detuned saw stack with a slow phasing growl, dark and wide: drum and bass and deep house.

name: Wobble Bass
about: Saw bass whose filter wobbles in eighth notes at the Project tempo.

name: Log Drum Bass
about: Amapiano log drum: a woody, pitched knock that drops into its note and decays quickly.

name: Supersaw Lead
about: Seven detuned saws: the bright, wide trance and big-room lead.

name: Chip Square
about: Bare square or pulse wave with no filter, like a game console sound chip.

name: Sync Lead
about: Hard-synced saw whose overtones sweep down at each note: a biting 80s lead.

name: Hoover
about: Rave hoover: a detuned pulse-saw stack that scoops up into each note with a sub octave.

name: Synth Brass
about: Polysynth brass stab: saw chords whose filter swells open, then settles.

name: String Machine
about: Ensemble string machine: chorused saws with a slow bowed attack and thin low end.

name: Analog Pad
about: Warm, slow polysynth pad that breathes with a slow filter LFO.

name: FM Bell
about: Bright two-operator FM bell at a 3.5:1 ratio, clangy at the strike and ringing pure.

name: FM Tines
about: FM electric piano: a mellow body with a short metallic tine bark that grows with velocity.

name: Rave Stab
about: Minor-seventh chord on every key: a snappy filtered rave and house stab.

name: Noise Riser
about: Filtered noise sweep that rises while the key is held: a build-up effect.

name: Boom Kick
about: Long, pitched 808-style boom: a swept sine you can play as a bass line.

name: Punch Kick
about: Short, punchy 909-style kick with a fast pitch drop and a beater click.

name: Machine Snare
about: 808-style snare: two tuned tones under a bright noise burst.

name: Snap Snare
about: 909-style snare: noisier, snappier and brighter than the 808.

name: Machine Clap
about: 808-style clap: staggered noise bursts with a short room-like tail.

name: Machine Cowbell
about: 808-style cowbell: two square waves at 540 and 800 Hz through a band-pass.

name: Machine Hat
about: 808-style closed hat: six detuned square waves through a high band-pass.

name: Machine Open Hat
about: 808-style open hat: the same metallic squares with a long decay.

name: Machine Tom
about: Analog drum-machine tom: a pitched, swept sine you can tune across the keys.

name: Kit Toms
about: Acoustic rack and floor toms, tuned across the keys from floor (low) to high rack.

name: China Cymbal
about: Trashy, bright China cymbal with a fast, rattly decay.

name: Ride Bell
about: Bell of a ride cymbal: a clear, pinging metallic tone over a little wash.

name: Cajón
about: Flamenco cajón: deep bass tone up to C4, snare-wire slap above C4.

name: Darbuka
about: Goblet drum: resonant doum up to C4, sharp tek at the rim above C4.

name: Frame Drum
about: Hand frame drum (bodhrán, tar): soft low boom up to C4, bright rim above C4.

name: Taiko
about: Japanese taiko: a huge low don up to C4, a rim ka click above C4.

name: Udu
about: Nigerian clay pot drum: an airy, rising bass bloop up to C4, a clay tap above C4.

name: Talking Drum
about: West African talking drum: each stroke bends up in pitch as the cords are squeezed.

name: Agogô
about: Brazilian double bell: low bell up to C4, high bell above C4.

name: Guiro
about: Scraped gourd: a long down-scrape up to C4, a short flick above C4.

name: Cuíca
about: Brazilian friction drum: a squeaking, sliding laugh; low up to C4, high above C4.

name: Sleigh Bells
about: A shaken strap of small jingle bells.

name: Temple Blocks
about: Hollow wooden temple blocks, tuned across the keys.

name: Slit Drum
about: Wooden slit or log drum: a short, round, pitched knock.

name: Vibraslap
about: The rattling buzz of a vibraslap's loose teeth in a wooden box.

name: Mark Tree
about: Hand sweep across a mark tree's small chimes: upward up to C4, downward above C4.

name: Steel Pan
about: Trinidadian tenor steel pan: a sweet, slightly beating metallic note with octave overtones.

name: Handpan
about: Handpan (hang): soft, long-ringing steel notes with octave and twelfth overtones.

name: Singing Bowl
about: Struck Tibetan singing bowl: long ringing tone that slowly beats.

name: Gamelan Saron
about: Javanese saron: a bronze bar struck with a mallet, nearly pure and short.

name: Gamelan Bonang
about: Javanese bonang: a small bronze kettle gong, gong-like and slightly beating.

name: Music Box
about: Music box comb: tiny, pure plucked metal tines with a mechanical click.

name: Opera Gong
about: Chinese opera gong: a small gong whose pitch slides down slightly as it rings.

name: Banjo
about: Five-string banjo: a bright, twangy pluck with a short drum-head body.

name: Mandolin
about: Mandolin: paired steel strings, bright and short.

name: Ukulele
about: Ukulele: soft, short nylon pluck with a small body.

name: Clean Electric
about: Clean electric guitar: a long, round single-coil pluck without amp drive.

name: Crunch Guitar
about: Electric guitar through an overdriven amp and cabinet: crunchy and sustained.

name: Fretless Bass
about: Fretless electric bass: a warm, singing tone with a slight growl.

name: Sitar
about: Sitar: a buzzing bright pluck from the curved jawari bridge, with sympathetic strings ringing.

name: Koto
about: Japanese koto: a clear, bright silk-string pluck with a long ring.

name: Shamisen
about: Japanese shamisen: a percussive plectrum snap on a skin body with a buzzing sawari.

name: Oud
about: Middle Eastern oud: warm, fretless paired-string pluck with a deep body.

name: Hammered Dulcimer
about: Hammered dulcimer (santur, cimbalom): bright, ringing struck string courses.

name: Erhu
about: Chinese two-string fiddle: a nasal, expressive bowed tone with a wide vibrato.

name: Hurdy-Gurdy
about: Hurdy-gurdy: a wheel-bowed melody string over fixed G drones.

name: Tremolo Strings
about: String section playing tremolo: rapid, shimmering bow strokes.

name: Alto Sax
about: Alto saxophone: a reedy, vocal tone with a jazz vibrato.

name: Tenor Sax
about: Tenor saxophone: warmer and breathier than the alto.

name: Baritone Sax
about: Baritone saxophone: a big, honking low reed.

name: English Horn
about: English horn (cor anglais): a darker, mellower oboe.

name: Bass Clarinet
about: Bass clarinet: a woody, hollow low reed with odd harmonics.

name: Contrabassoon
about: Contrabassoon: the orchestra's lowest reed, dark and buzzy.

name: Recorder
about: Alto recorder: a simple, pure flute tone with a soft chiff.

name: Pan Flute
about: Pan flute: breathy, airy pipes with a soft attack.

name: Shakuhachi
about: Japanese bamboo flute: a very breathy, expressive tone that scoops into notes.

name: Bansuri
about: Indian bamboo flute: breathy and warm with a gentle vibrato.

name: Ocarina
about: Ocarina: an almost pure, round, hollow tone.

name: Duduk
about: Armenian duduk: a mellow, plaintive double reed.

name: Harmonica
about: Harmonica: a bright, buzzy free reed that bends into notes.

name: Accordion
about: Accordion with a musette register: three slightly detuned reeds that beat.

name: Bagpipes
about: Bagpipes: a loud, reedy chanter over fixed A drones.

name: Didgeridoo
about: Didgeridoo: a buzzing low drone whose vowel shifts as the player moves the mouth.

name: Flugelhorn
about: Flugelhorn: a softer, darker, rounder trumpet.

name: Muted Trumpet
about: Trumpet with a harmon mute: thin, nasal and buzzy.

name: Euphonium
about: Euphonium: a mellow, round tenor brass.

name: Bass Trombone
about: Bass trombone: a heavy, dark low brass.

name: Drawbar Organ
about: Tonewheel organ with percussion and key click through a fast rotary speaker.

name: Tape Flute
about: Tape-replay flute keyboard: wobbly, lo-fi flute notes that stop after eight seconds.

name: Tape Strings
about: Tape-replay strings: a small, wobbly string ensemble that stops after eight seconds.

name: Glass Harmonica
about: Glass harmonica: pure, ethereal tones of rubbed glass with a slow swell.

name: Honky-Tonk
about: Honky-tonk upright: a piano with its string courses noticeably out of tune with each other.

name: Prepared Piano
about: Prepared piano: dull, muted strings with bolts and rattles in them.

name: Choir Oohs
about: Mixed choir singing a soft 'oo'.

name: Soprano Voice
about: Solo operatic soprano singing 'ah' with a wide vibrato.

name: Bass Voice
about: Solo bass singer on a deep 'oh'.
